questions.q: What are the three main roles that nutrients play in our body?
questions.a: Nutrients provide energy, support body-building (growth/repair), and protect the body from diseases. An answer that only mentions "energy" reveals that the student is ignoring the vital "protective" and "building" functions of food.

questions.q: If someone only eats rice every day, why is their diet not "balanced"?
questions.a: While rice provides energy (carbohydrates), it lacks sufficient protein for repair and protective vitamins/minerals. A student answering "because they will get fat" misses the point of nutrition, focusing only on weight instead of the lack of variety in essential nutrients.

questions.q: If you have a plate with roti, dal, a little ghee, and spinach, which components are you providing for your body?
questions.a: Roti provides carbohydrates, dal provides protein, ghee provides fat, and spinach provides vitamins/minerals. A student who misses one component fails to recognize the specific function of common Indian food ingredients.

questions.q: Compare a packet of potato wafers with a bowl of roasted chana. Why is one considered "junk food" while the other is a healthier snack?
questions.a: Potato wafers are high in fat/sugar but low in nutrients (vitamins/minerals/protein), while roasted chana is rich in protein and fibre. A student who says "wafers taste better" is confusing personal preference with nutritional value.

questions.q: Why is it important to eat fruits and vegetables in their raw or lightly cooked state when possible?
questions.a: Cooking at high heat can destroy sensitive nutrients like Vitamin C. A student who says "because it tastes better" is ignoring the chemical reality of nutrient degradation mentioned in the chapter.

questions.q: Design a simple, low-cost "balanced" lunch plate using local Indian staples.
questions.a: A good answer would include a cereal (e.g., rice or roti), a pulse (e.g., moong or tuar dal), and a seasonal vegetable (e.g., carrot or leafy greens). A poor answer would include items like "biscuits and soda," failing to meet the requirement for protein and protective nutrients.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A balanced diet is a daily food pattern that provides the body with the right proportions of energy-giving ______ and fats, body-building proteins, and protective vitamins and minerals, along with necessary dietary fibre and water.
Fill in the blank: Think about how you feel after eating a heavy meal of just sweets versus a meal with dal, roti, and ______.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to categorize food items by their primary nutrient role and justify why a meal choice contributes to or fails a balanced diet based on variety and proportionality.
